intended_object: A basis of the Clifford algebra Cl(M, Q), indexed by the finite subsets of the index set of a basis b of M. It is defined as the image of the standard exterior-algebra basis under the linear isomorphism Cl(Q) ≃ ⋀M, which exists when 2 is invertible (Chevalley). This is inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body maps Mathlib's basis `Module.Basis.ExteriorAlgebra` (indexed by `Finset I`) along `(CliffordAlgebra.equivExterior Q).symm`, which is an `R`-linear equivalence `ExteriorAlgebra R M ≃ₗ CliffordAlgebra Q`. Mapping a basis along a linear equivalence gives a basis, so the result is a genuine `R`-basis of `CliffordAlgebra Q` indexed by finite subsets, as the docstring says.

The docstring and the implementation notes say plainly that these elements are not, by definition, the ordered products `ι(b i₁)⋯ι(b iₖ)`, the textbook basis. So the definition does not claim to be that basis. Its purpose is to make the Clifford algebra free with rank 2^n, and it does that correctly.

The hypothesis `[Invertible (2 : R)]` is needed by this construction, because `equivExterior` is built from `changeForm` and needs 2 to be invertible. The textbook product basis exists for any free module over any commutative ring, but that would be a different construction, the PBW-type theorem the notes mention. A transport along `equivExterior` cannot be stated without this hypothesis, so it is not an unneeded restriction.

`LinearOrder I` is the hypothesis Mathlib's exterior-algebra basis uses. Mathlib has no basis of `CliffordAlgebra` in general, so nothing broader exists to compare against.
